| `components/c-status-route/responsibility` (line 68) | Append: "`ready` is boolean and true only when `state=ready`. `reason` and `fix` are strings, empty when ready. `account`, `upstream_host` and `quota.reset` are strings or null; `quota.usable` is boolean. `pid`, counters and model `max_prompt_tokens` are integers. `since` is epoch milliseconds of the last state change, not process uptime or the last check time." |
| Same status-route field | Append the failure mapping: "Missing config/account (or unreadable config) -> `no_account`; disabled -> `off`; missing gh -> `gh_missing`; token-fetch failure or readiness 401 -> `no_token`; no entitlement (user response without `endpoints.api`, or readiness 403/404) -> `quota_exhausted`; network/timeout/5xx failures -> `upstream_unreachable`." |
| Same status-route field | Expand reload: "POST reload takes no parameters from a request body: it rereads the config file, refetches when the account changed, no token is held or the last fetch/refresh failed, reruns readiness, and returns the status object." |

| `components/c-proxy-core/responsibility` (line 28) | Add: "Upstream redirects are not followed." Refine the rewrite wording to "add a missing TTL only to ephemeral cache controls on main-agent requests; preserve explicit TTLs", and specify that only client `X-Initiator: agent` or `user` wins; absent/other values use the documented last-user-message/all-tool-result inference. |
| `costs/k-3/rate` | Include the existing 60-second failed-check cache alongside the 10-minute successful cache, so the declared GET rate matches the same readiness rule. |
